title: Babur Asks for Hindustan and Is Directed Toward the Prophet

blocks.text: Having abandoned open defiance, Babur states his request plainly. He says he came because he was called and asks Guru Nanak to grant him the throne of Hindustan rather than leaving the matter hanging in hints and half-confessions.

Guru Nanak refuses to flatter that ambition in worldly language. If Babur claims kingship under God and appeals to pirs and prophets, then he must carry the question beyond politics and seek its answer through the higher court he himself invokes.

Babur accepts the rebuke and asks for a way to approach that reality. The page thus turns the scene away from conquest alone and toward an ascent in which imperial desire must pass through prophecy, submission, and spiritual testing.
